reason: Checked against the Project Gutenberg transcription (#13415) of Garnett’s The Lady with the Dog and Other Stories (1917): the quoted sentence matches the Garnett text word for word, including the semicolon and the comma in “long, long road”, and it is the final sentence of section IV, the last paragraph before A Doctor’s Visit begins. Not shipped, not near a shipped line, Chekhov not banned and at zero for the year. Source line leads with the name, no dash, 103 characters, Fiction is the form. Narrator’s sentence, so no speaker needed. One quibble that does not refute: Gutenberg does not name the publisher, so the evidence’s “Chatto and Windus, 1917” is an inference (Garnett’s 1917 volume appeared under Chatto and Windus in London and Macmillan in New York, same text); the source line itself only claims Garnett 1917, which is correct.
